rationale:
Slice B of bugs_open/151 candidate 1 — the CONSUMPTION half of plan-time fact assignment, plus candidate 1b, which the 2026-08-08 draft of this round was HELD pending. This is the round RFC_016 s3 defines and the guardian's round-1 veto (corr 902a8563) explicitly asked for. 

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE DRAFT, because it is the whole reason this is submittable now. The draft named two blockers. (1) bugs_open/215 — a canonicalised page-name collision killed the entire plan write — is FIXED, council-APPROVED round 1 (corr 8ab18991), live and artefact-verified on chassis v1.0.1276. (2) Candidate 1b was undesigned; it is now built, and it turned out to be the load-bearing part of this round rather than an addendum. 

WHY 1b IS NOT OPTIONAL. Slice A round 2 (corr 1cb17b11, 2026-08-08) proved the planner COMPLIES with seed 333 at the emission — object form with facts on effectively every composed page — and then proved the assignments never survive validate_plan on a DEPLOYED page. An assignment travels INSIDE its section entry, and reconcilePlanWithRealised's Pass B/B2 restore a built page's realised composition by replacing the LLM's entries wholesale, so the assignments were discarded with them. Without 1b, Slice B would wire a consumption path that can only ever reach pages built AFTER their plan first carried assignments — never the already-built pages (index, capabilities, about) that hold the nine fact-overlap pairs that motivated bug 151 in the first place. The acceptance criterion of this round would have been unreachable and we would not have known why. 

1b HAS TWO HALVES AND THEY ARE DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC. (ii), the Go half, re-attaches assignments onto the restored entries by component NAME — the only identity the two lists share, since the realised list is plain strings and ordering and length differ; position is not an address that survives, per RFC_016 s1a. It is committed (f611dde6a) and is submitted here for review, not for permission: on this tree HEAD is shared and any session's roll ships it, which the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 states is by design. (i), the prompt half, is seed 362 and is HELD with this round's other seeds. With 362 applied the planner re-emits the realised list, the composition compares EQUAL, and nothing is restored or carried at all — (ii) becomes the safety net rather than the mechanism, and its FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION rows become a measure of planner disobedience rather than of a structural gap. 

CONSUMERS TOLD, NOT MERELY MEASURED (owner ruling 2026-07-29 s3). reconcilePlanWithRealised is the re-plan preservation guard for every site, not this lane's function. Its guarantee — a built page's composition survives a re-plan — is UNCHANGED and is pinned by all 15 pre-existing tests, which pass unmodified. What changes for its other consumers is the counter: snapped_sections now counts composition changes again, which is what its name has always claimed. It had silently stopped doing so when seed 333 shipped, with no code change — see the risks block. 

REMAINING GATES, stated so the round is judged against the real sequence: the human/compliance read of the v4 writer plaintext (committed at brochure_component_library/sql/page_content_writer_prompt_v4_2026-08-06.txt, the compliance seat's round-1 ask) happens BEFORE seed 330 applies; apply order is 362, then 328, then 330; the acceptance is a replan plus a rebuild of fundamentallyai's flagged pages, then the overlap census — pairs must fall on engaged pages, and the five fact-blind sites must NOT move, which is the disconfirming half.

plan.summary: Wire the consumption half of plan-time fact assignment, and fix the reason it could not reach a built page. Consumption: page-build-handler passes each ready section's assigned facts to the writer (seed 328, opt-in step-config key), and writer prompt v4 branches on current_section.facts_scoped — scoped sections state ONLY their assigned facts, '[]' sections state none, unscoped sections keep today's site-wide block byte-identically (seed 330). Candidate 1b: carrySectionFactsOntoRealised re-attaches assignments onto a built page's restored composition by component name, misses recorded durably as FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION, and seed 362 shows the planner the realised section list so the match is near-total rather than coincidental. Seed 333 (planner: object form mandatory per page, owner decision RFC_016 s5.3) is included for review although already applied, so the round covers the full prompt breadth the guardian vetoed shipping unreviewed.

edits.rationale: The carry itself. Matching is by component NAME because that is the only identity the two lists share: the realised list is plain strings, ordering and length differ, and a positional cross-reference that outlives the state it counted is the defect RFC_016 s1a names (and bugs_open/214 is living proof of, on the imagery wire). A name may repeat on a page — two text blocks — so assignments queue per name and the Nth realised entry of a name takes the Nth assignment, rather than all of them collapsing onto slot one. The result is emitted in the planner's OWN object form, so nothing new has to understand it: validate_plan's normalise pass splits it exactly as it splits the planner's own emission. When nothing carries, the realised slice is returned UNCHANGED — that is what keeps every pre-seed-333 plan byte-identical, and it is asserted, not assumed.

The two sites of the loss. Pass B2 (same name, composition changed) is the one RFC_016 s3b measured. Pass B (renamed page snapping back to a realised identity) was flagged as UNESTABLISHED in the handoff and turned out to lose assignments the same way one pass earlier — its other branch, the un-shipped catalogued page, already keeps the LLM's entries whole and so needed nothing. The third branch, a DEPLOYED sectionless page forced back to empty (bugs_open/050), cannot carry anything because there is no section to carry onto; it records what it discarded instead, since a planner scoping facts to a page that has no sections is a prompt fault worth seeing. The five positional int returns became a named struct in the same edit: two more counters on a positional return is how the next one goes wrong quietly, and this function had just demonstrated that failure mode.

A correction, not a refinement, and the reviewers should weigh it as the most surprising thing in this round. The predicate compared whole entries with fmt.Sprintf("%v", ...). Once seed 333 made the planner emit OBJECTS against a realised list of plain STRINGS, %v of a map never equals %v of a string, so every composed page compared 'changed': snapped_sections silently stopped counting composition changes and started counting shape differences, and each one forced a restore over a list that was already identical. No Go changed to cause that — a row in agent_definitions did. Comparing by section name restores the counter's meaning and, as a side effect, makes the equal-composition case free: the planner's entries stay, so their assignments survive with no carry at all. Filed as a LANDMINE because the general form is that a live prompt edit can redefine a Go metric between two reads of it.

The durable half, and the reason it is durable rather than a log line: a name match that matches NOTHING produces exactly the plan a working carry produces, so pod output is the only thing that could ever tell them apart — and it does not survive long enough to ask afterwards (chassis logs rotate fast; the orchestration row holding collected_data is pruned at ~24h, which this lane has already been bitten by). agent_error_log is the channel plan_sections already uses for FACT_SCOPING_EMPTY_COMPOSITION, the sibling anomaly one step later in this same feature, so querying both by error_code answers 'did assignment reach the writer, and where did it stop?'. Best-effort by construction: a failed write must not change the plan the validator already decided.

Candidate 1b (i). The planner was already GIVEN this data — existing_pages is an input_field of plan_site and load_existing_pages already selects p.sections — the prompt simply never printed it. So the planner could not know what a built page is composed of, re-composed it freely, and (since seed 333 made assignment mandatory per section) attached its assignments to names the built page does not have. The last sentence of the addition is deliberate and load-bearing: recompose_pages releases a page from the preservation guard and the planner is not told which pages those are, so an unconditional 'always re-emit' would silently defeat deliberate redesign. Anchors derived byte-exact from a fresh dump, never retyped.
edits.sketch:
{{range .existing_pages}}- name: {{.name}} | page_type: {{.page_type}} | url: {{.url}}
+{{if .sections}} | sections: {{.sections}}{{end}}

  ...Do not invent placeholder or example pages such as "post".
+ Each existing page is listed with the "sections:" it is actually built from. That composition is
+ preserved when the plan is validated, so for a page shown with a section list, re-emit that exact
+ list, in that order, as its "sections" array — do not re-compose it and do not substitute similar
+ component names. This matters for fact assignment (RULES, rule 17): an assignment travels inside
+ the section entry you emit, so a fact you attach to a section name this page does not have is
+ discarded silently. Put each carried-over page's fact assignments on the section names shown for
+ it. A page shown as "sections: []" is rendered by another part of the system — emit an empty
+ "sections" array for it and assign it no facts. Only when the briefing explicitly asks for a page
+ to be redesigned should you propose a different composition for it, and then its fact assignments
+ must name the NEW sections.

Makes the object form mandatory for EVERY section of EVERY page when a roster exists, so NULL assignments on a fact-rich site now mean the planner disobeyed rather than 'was allowed to skip'. That is what turns the follow-up replan into a compliance check — and it is also what made 1b necessary, because a compliant planner assigning facts to a built page it re-composed produces assignments that cannot land.

Guardian veto, round 1 (corr 902a8563, 2026-08-06): rejection on BREADTH not correctness — 'three simultaneous fleet-wide prompt changes plus four Go files in one submission'; this round is the sliced consumption half it asked for, plus the one Go change that half cannot work without.
Owner decisions 2026-08-08 (RFC_016 s5): section-entry rule RATIFIED (with s1a scope clarification), sliced order APPROVED, s3a decided for option (a).

bugs_open/215 (the draft's second blocker) CLOSED in substance: council APPROVED round 1 (corr 8ab18991, 3 advisory objections, none high-severity), commit 14b1cff28, artefact-verified on chassis v1.0.1276 — 4 positives to 1 on both replicas, negative control 'collapsed after canonicalization' (US spelling) to 0.

Ordering claim behind 1b, verified by reading the caller rather than assumed: reconcilePlanWithRealised is called at ValidateSitePlanAction:3101 and the object-form normalise pass runs at :3277 — 176 lines later, same function body. Therefore object form emitted by the carry never escapes validate_plan, and the 15+ non-test readers of pages["sections"] are NOT in the blast radius. Pinned end to end by TestValidateSitePlan_CarriedFactsLeaveAsStringsPlusSectionFacts, not by the argument.

The two loops between the reconcile and the normalise (chrome-strip at :3177, component-name resolution at :3220) already read either shape via sectionEntryName, and the resolution loop explicitly preserves an object entry's other keys — read, not assumed, before emitting object form into that window.

Consumption is genuinely zero today, measured with a positive control because a bare zero over jsonb::text LIKE is exactly the shape that lies: agent_definitions matching section_facts / facts_scoped / assigned_fact_ids = 0 / 0 / 0, against 185 live agents, with the same predicate proved able to match (workflow 186, evidence_base 9). So 1b (ii) changes only how many assignments are STORED; nothing reads them until the two seeds in this round apply.

1b (ii) is mutation-tested, because a name match that matches nothing produces the same plan as one that works: four mutations introduced against a clean `git archive HEAD` overlay and each caught by the right test — a no-op carry (5 tests fail), a swallowed miss (only the 2 miss assertions fail, hits still pass), the old %v comparison (the counter test fails), and a silently discarded assignment on a deployed sectionless page.

All 15 pre-existing reconcilePlanWithRealised tests pass UNMODIFIED apart from the mechanical struct-return change, which is the evidence that the preservation guarantee this function exists for is untouched.

Seed 362 is proven, not assumed: a forced-rollback dry run against the live row applied cleanly (anchor counts 1/1, UPDATE 1, both verify assertions passed), and the verify block was proven able to FAIL by mutating one replacement out — it raised '362: verify failed — the re-emit instruction is missing'. The live row is unchanged by either run (18,738 bytes, no '| sections: ' present).

Go half of Slice A live: v1.0.1262 pod-verified both replicas 2026-08-07 ('assigned fact id matches no current evidence_base fact'->1, 'fact assignment composed an empty writer block'->1, removed extractSectionNames->0, positive control diagnose_persist_fix_plan->10).

Empty-composition degradation (round-1 bug_historian objection, fixed in code): a non-empty assignment resolving to zero known facts degrades to UNSCOPED plus a durable agent_error_log row FACT_SCOPING_EMPTY_COMPOSITION, with an sqlmock test asserting the INSERT (commit ff515351e). FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION is deliberately the same channel one step earlier.
plan.risks:
THE ONE A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK FIRST — object form now exists in a window it did not before. The carry emits the planner's object form into pages["sections"] BETWEEN the reconcile (:3101) and the normalise pass (:3277). Everything downstream of validate_plan still sees plain strings, and the two loops inside that window read either shape via sectionEntryName. But that is a claim about a 176-line window in one function, and if the normalise pass were ever moved above the reconcile, or an early return were added between them, object form would escape into sync_pages_to_db and into pages.sections, whose every reader expects strings. The end-to-end test fails loudly if that happens; a reviewer who thinks a comment is insufficient protection here is not wrong, and the honest answer is that the test is the control, not the comment.

THE COUNTER CHANGED MEANING AND NO CODE DID IT. snapped_sections has been counting shape differences rather than composition changes since seed 333 shipped, because sameSectionList compared whole entries with %v. Any figure read across that boundary is two measurements with one name. This round corrects it; it does not retro-correct anything already recorded, and nothing in this lane's docs quotes such a figure. Filed as a LANDMINE, footprinted on the symbol, because the general form — a live prompt edit redefining a Go metric with no build — will recur on any counter whose predicate compares LLM output structurally.

THE PROMPT HALF INTERACTS WITH DELIBERATE REDESIGN. Seed 362 tells the planner to re-emit a built page's realised sections verbatim. recompose_pages exists precisely to redesign such a page, and it releases it from the preservation guard — but the planner is NOT told which pages are on that list, so the instruction carries an explicit escape ('only when the briefing explicitly asks for a page to be redesigned'). That escape is prose, and prose is a weaker control than a field. It is the strongest available without plumbing recompose_pages into the prompt, which is a bigger change than this round should carry; a reviewer who wants that plumbing should say so and it becomes a follow-up.

MISS RECORDS WILL APPEAR, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING. Once 362 applies, a FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION row means the planner disobeyed the re-emit instruction, not that the carry is broken. Before 362 applies, rows are expected and measure the structural gap. Do not read the row count as a defect rate without saying which side of 362 it was taken on.

THE CONSUMPTION FLIP, unchanged from the draft. It changes what the writer is TOLD on scoped sections only; the unscoped arm must remain byte-identical to today's behaviour — check the v4 template's else-branch reproduces the v3 writer_block injection exactly (the committed plaintext makes that a line diff). Rebuilds after apply rewrite scoped sections' prose: on fact-rich sites that is the intended effect (dedup), on fact-blind sites nothing changes (facts_scoped never set — their five census scores are the no-move control). A planner that disobeys rule 17 produces NULL assignments, which fall into the unscoped arm = today's behaviour, so disobedience fails SAFE.

APPLY ORDER MATTERS: 362, then 328, then 330 (a v4 prompt without the wiring key sees no facts_scoped and behaves as v3); all after the human read of the v4 plaintext. Known defect deliberately out of scope: imagery scope_ref orphans (bugs_open/214, filed with census and fix candidates) — same wire, different field; its fix does not gate this round.
